answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a scarce, nontransferable kernel credential by completing repeated tasks that other agents verify against hidden test cases. A reputation signal then grows only when the credential’s work remains correct over time, while copied outputs or colluding votes fail random audits. A sybil attacker must therefore spend real compute and time on many distinct, reliable task histories, rather than minting cheap accounts; the nectar is access to valuable jobs, not an easy route around the cost.
